business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong regulatory overlay; administered as part of China for international purposes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) - Trade in Services Annex (as applicable)
Agreement Between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and the Straits Exchange Foundation on the Establishment of the Mechanism for Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3: Administrative Measures for the Beneficial Owner Information Registration of Legal Entities and Other Organizations (effective November 1, 2024); PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2018 Revision, as amended by the 2020 Decision); PRC Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises' Establishment and Change Filing (SAMR Order No. 51); Taiwan (China) Company Act and Money Laundering Control Act (when dealing with Taiwan-registered counterparties); SAMR Provisions on Name Registration for Enterprises; SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization and authentication arrangements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate) of the ultimate parent or overseas shareholder company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single-track Hague Apostille if issuing registry is in an Apostille Convention state; otherwise, notarization by local notary public, then authentication by the competent ministry of foreign affairs of the country of origin, then consular legalization by the Consular Office of the Embassy/Consulate of China in that jurisdiction (do not combine with Apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant Registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If Hong Kong (which applies the Apostille Convention): Apostille by Hong Kong High Court Registry; for other jurisdictions: apostille from the country's designated competent authority where a member state, or full consular legalization chain (notary, MOFA, Chinese consulate) where a non-member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE incorporation agent, fixing the registered capital amount and appointing the first legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or sole shareholder of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate act executed before a notary; legalization via Apostille or Consular route depending exclusively on the country of execution; if executed in Taiwan, cross-strait notarization through SEF and ARATS may be required in lieu of consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the foreign parent entity (full certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the designated national competent authority if the issuer is a Hague Convention signatory; otherwise notarization followed by consular authentication by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; must not be doubly chained

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the shareholder's banking relationships and clean AML/CFT standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or account-holding bank of the beneficial owner/foreign parent in its home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank's branch notarization followed by either Apostille (for member states) or consular legalization (for non-member states, e.g., certain jurisdictions where Taiwan offices exist independent of Chinese consulates; in such cases the document must be routed through the cross-strait notarization mechanism)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Residential/Registered Address Proof of each direct shareholder and the ultimate beneficial owner (e.g., utility bill, bank statement, or corporate address certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility, bank, or competent directory authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path independent of the other instruments: Apostille if the residence country is a Hague Contracting State; otherwise notarize and obtain certificate of authentication from the competent national authority, then Chinese consular legalization; never Apostille plus consular legalization consecutively

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The corporate service provider must conduct, before any filing, real-time screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Chinese Ministry of Public Security blacklists, PBOC penalty and UBO databases, the PRC SAMR named-person registries, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the consolidated European Union financial sanctions list, the United States OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (including sectoral sanctions), and the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any politically exposed person is identified in relation to aviation spare parts resale or where any source of funds is connected to Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan Special Administrative Region family trusts or relay corporate structures. The firm must also search bankruptcy, disqualification, civil judgments, and customs enforcement records; obtain a negative media report from at least two independent global databases; verify the source of wealth through documentary evidence such as audited financial statements, sales contracts, and escrow payment flows; and reject any client that cannot demonstrate a lawful and transparent value chain for surplus military-derived or end-user-restricted commercial aircraft parts. A risk rating of at least Medium-Risk Enhanced must be assigned under the PRC PBOC Category-II obliged entity rules, with transaction monitoring escalation to the SAMR anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing office where any unusual pattern appears in the proposed licensing application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: China SAMR Enterprise Name Registration Online Platform (national enterprise credit information public announcement system and the SAMR enterprise name autonomous declaration system, administered through local Administration for Market Regulation; practical filing portal: www.gsxt.gov.cn and the provincial SAIC/SAMR autonomous name-selection modules)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters and may include Arabic numerals or Roman letters only as technically permitted for the industry suffix. The proposed name must comprise four tiers: (1) administrative division (e.g., Shanghai municipality or city name), (2) distinctive trade mark or invented name, (3) industry description that must match the approved business scope (e.g., aviation materials sales or aerospace parts trade), and (4) statutory organizational form suffix 'limited company'. English names are voluntary but must be registered separately in the foreign-invested entity filing; where a Chinese transliteration of a foreign shareholder's name is used, it must follow the standard phonetic transliteration prescribed by the SAMR and the Chinese State Language Commission, avoiding identical characters with known national leaders, famous public institutions, or famous trademarks without authorization. The applicant must verify that the pinyin or Roman-letter form does not create a conflict with an existing enterprise on the national database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a rejection notice from the SAMR name registration system, the applicant must, within the statutory review period (typically 15 working days from the rejection), submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the local Administration for Market Regulation that issued the decision, or, in the case of automated system rejection, apply for manual review through the 'hard-case enterprise name' channel. The appeal application must include the original application number, the rejected name in Chinese, a legal identity certificate of the proposed legal representative, an explanation of the distinctive elements and how they are not identical or deceptively similar to prohibited names or prior registered marks, and evidence of the absence of conflicts on the SAMR national database. If the administrative reconsideration authority upholds the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. As an alternative, the applicant may simultaneously reserve up to three backup names and designate the next acceptable name to avoid operational delay; the backup name is subject to the same screening under the PBOC/SAMR UBO rules when the incorporation filing is ultimately submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared co-working postal address without a physical fixed office that can receive correspondence, host original corporate documents, and accommodate tax and customs inspections is not permissive for a WFOE whose business scope is distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus. The PRC Foreign Investment Law and the SAMR registration rules require the registered address to be the actual operational address; the local tax authority and customs officers may require proof that the address corresponds to a real place where the company's seal, accounting books, inventory inspection facilities, and licensed aviation parts documentation are kept. Some cities (e.g., Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone and certain Qianhai/Shenzhen zones) allow 'address hosting' or 'one-site multiple-licenses' under special policies, but banks and customs brokers will generally require a physical anchor, a dedicated office lease of at least 12 months, an on-site staff member, and a visible company signboard. For the aviation parts trading industry, the SAMR and the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) confirm the business scope only upon documentary proof that the registered premises include a secure storage area for dual-use and end-user documentation if the parts are imported on consignment. Therefore, a virtual office is rejected for this industry for tax invoice issuance, export VAT refund, and CAAC licensing, while a 'registered-address-only but managed physical site in a permitted zone' arrangement is acceptable only if a supplementary actual office is reported to the tax authority under the social credit filing system.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist of inspection triggers: 1) first six-month post-incorporation verification by the district SAMR office; 2) annual corporate information report mismatches (double declaration of registered address vs actual address); 3) issuance of export VAT invoices where customs records show no physical storage; 4) application for CAAC import or distribution license; 5) unusual volume of cross-strait (Taiwan-China) aviation parts purchase orders or involvement of Taiwan-licensed airline maintenance organizations; 6) complaints from neighbouring tenant companies or property management about lack of occupancy; 7) ESPECIALLY: exporter flagging under PBOC enhanced AML category due to high-value parts and escrow payments from cyber-adjacent countries; 8) a UBO whose beneficial ownership chain files a beneficial owner statement with Taiwan bank accounts that does not correspond to the mainland registered premises. Quantified risk: for a Company Limited with actual business activity and a compliant physical lease, the probability of an unannounced inspection in the first year is approximately 15% to 25% by municipal market regulation authorities; if the registered address is a virtual service address, the probability rises to 70% to 80%, with a statutory ordering to rectify within 30 days and a potential fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000 and cancellation of the registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chinese Government does not impose a statutory filing fee for enterprise name clearance; processing is provided as a free electronic administrative service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee per PRC Administrative Charges Catalogue: RMB 0 for LLC registration for ordinary trading companies; incidental certificate printing or e-certificate download free.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: PBOC/SAMR implements the UBO registration as an integrated zero-fee administrative procedure for the first filing within mandated deadline; professional service fee is separately incurred.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of parent company board resolution and power of attorney for the incorporation agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hong Kong notarial fee benchmark HKD 2,000-3,000 per board resolution witness plus binder; Singapore notary public fee SGD 150-250 per document; translated into USD average 250-450 per corporate set.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of notarized corporate documents from a Hague Convention competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong High Court Registry / Singapore Ministry of Law or corresponding apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard apostille fee per brochure: Hong Kong HKD 125 per document; Singapore SGD 10 per apostille for specific document categories; market courier and processing aggregate USD 80-150.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of Chinese official documents or non-Hague jurisdiction parent documents (if Taiwan parent or mainland notarization is involved)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese Embassy / Consulate or SEF-ARATS cross-strait notarization mechanism (as applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chinese consular fee schedule plus agency facilitation fee; typical combined cost for one commercial document in non-Apostille routing USD 120-300 consular fee plus courier and translator.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of all foreign-language company documents (Articles of Association, Certificate of Good Standing, UBO evidence, board resolutions) by a SAMR-recognized translation bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed certified translation company in Shanghai/Beijing or in the jurisdiction where notarization occurred
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate RMB 150-350 per 1,000 Chinese characters plus certification stamp; estimated for 8-12 document pages aggregate translation cost USD 250-400.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR standard seal engraving authorization and production of five statutory seals (official seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, invoice seal, contract seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local public security bureau-authorized seal engraving service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: PRC Public Security regulations set a maximum administrative guidance price; industry standard RMB 1,100-1,500 per set in first-tier cities for anti-counterfeit chip seals; quote USD 150-200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office lease deposit and first month's rent for a compliant office in a SAMR-permitted zone (Shanghai or Xiamen pilot zone) with commercial substance for aviation parts storage

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Chapter II Limited Company, Articles 1, 7, 12, 15, 23, 98 to 116, 128 to 151 and 156, together with the Foreign Investment Act Articles 4, 6 and 8, and the Civil Aviation Act Articles 40 and 44 insofar as imported airworthy aircraft components are distributed with release certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, for foreign investment approval, and the One-Stop Business Registration Center, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, for statutory company incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation of a Limited Company and the Company Establishment Registration Application prescribed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Taiwan Company Act. The wholly foreign-owned limited liability company must nevertheless declare a paid-up capital reasonably sufficient for its ISIC 4659 aviation spares distribution business, deposit the entire subscription money into a company bank account, and submit a bank capital certificate with the incorporation filing. No blocked escrow account or fixed capital floor is imposed by the general company registration regime, provided the foreign investment approval has been obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company, a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company proposed to be organized under the laws of Taiwan, was held on the date and at the address stated in the convening notice, with all directors present in person or by proxy. The chair confirmed that a quorum existed and that all directors had waived formal notice in writing. After due discussion, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously adopted. 1. Approval of Capital Subscription and Share Allotment. The Board approved the issue and allotment of ordinary shares with par value specified in the Articles of Incorporation, for an aggregate subscribed paid-up capital as set out in the subscription schedule. The founding shareholder shall pay the full subscription price in cash into a corporate bank account opened in the Company's name, and the bank certificate of deposit shall be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs as part of the incorporation registration. 2. Adoption and Confirmation of Registered Office. The Board adopted the registered office and principal place of business described in the Articles of Incorporation, located in Taipei, Taiwan. The Company is authorized to execute and file the registered office declaration, lease instruments, building safety-use documentation and utility applications required to establish the office and the bonded or non-bonded warehouse. 3. Banking Authorization. The Board authorized the Company to open corporate transaction, escrow and SWIFT wire-receiving accounts with a licensed Taiwanese bank. The Chairman, General Manager and Finance Director, acting jointly in any combination of two, shall have signatory power. The Board specifically authorized execution of banking mandates, indemnity agreements, escrow deponential instructions and wire transfer protocol forms for aviation parts purchase and sale transactions. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board unanimously appointed the Chairman, General Manager, Company Secretary and a Taiwan certified public accountant as auditor, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until earlier replacement. The General Manager is authorized, on behalf of the Company, to apply for all operating licenses, including the aviation supplier authorization, foreign trade registration, environmental registrations, civil defense fire safety permits and occupational safety approvals necessary for the distribution and warehousing of surplus commercial aircraft parts. 5. Delegation of Administrative and Regulatory Actions. The Board delegated to the Company Secretary and external corporate counsel the duty to prepare, sign and submit the Company registration application, pay statutorily prescribed fees, respond to registry queries and obtain the certificate of incorporation. The Board declared all resolutions effective immediately and without further shareholder action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval Prior to Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The non-resident founding shareholder must file the Foreign Investment Approval application with the Investment Commission before submission of the company registration. The application is to be executed by the shareholder or by a duly notarized and legalized power of attorney appointing a local incorporator. The filing must include a complete business plan describing the ISIC 4659 distribution of certified surplus civil aircraft parts and avionics, the anticipated warehouse location, the proposed paid-up capital and the beneficial ownership chain. The Commission reviews the negative-list and national security screening. Since 100 percent foreign ownership is permitted for ordinary trading operations, the approval letter is generally issued after satisfactory compliance. Any query must be answered in writing within 15 days; an adverse decision may be contested through a motion for reconsideration to the Investment Commission within one month.
required_dossiers: Notarized or apostilled passport or certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the local incorporator
Business plan for surplus commercial aircraft parts distribution
Draft Articles of Incorporation and proposed paid-up capital schedule
Evidence of registered office lease or property title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant has 15 days to submit supplementary documents; if denied, the applicant may file a reconsideration with the Investment Commission or restructure the shareholding or business scope and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: One-Stop Business Registration Center, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company name must be reserved online through the One-Stop Business Registration Portal. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Taiwanese company name. At least two alternative names should be pre-selected. The business scope must be stated in professional English as wholesale and brokerage of machinery and equipment, comprising certified civil aircraft rotables, avionics and surplus airframe parts, together with supply chain storage and testing services. The online pre-check validates the business scope against the ISIC and regulatory schedules and instantly returns a name reservation receipt. The reservation is valid for six months and may be renewed once. If the name is rejected for resemblance or prohibited wording, the applicant may either select a new name or file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, the Company may resubmit with a modified distinguishing name or object to the administrative authority within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: One-Stop Business Registration Center, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment approval and the name reservation, the incorporator must file the Company Establishment Registration Application electronically through the MOEA portal. The Articles of Incorporation, subscription list, board meeting minutes and directors' written consents must be signed and notarized or legalized if executed outside Taiwan. The application must include the bank-issued paid-up capital certificate dated within five working days, the registered office proof, the auditor consent and the exact corporate governance appointments. The registry verifies the legality of the limited company structure and the sufficiency of the foreign investment approval. If all documents are in order, the MOEA issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Any deficiency must be cured by letter of variation within 15 days; an unreasonable refusal may be challenged by an administrative appeal within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or title evidence
Power of attorney for the authorized incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The applicant may submit a supplementary declaration within 15 days of a query; if registration is refused or suspended, the applicant may appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days and, if necessary, obtain a judicial remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Foreign Trade Merchant Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan, and Bureau of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, the Company must apply to the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration, VAT registration and unified invoice issuance. In the same filing cycle, the Company must register as an importer and exporter with the Bureau of Foreign Trade to obtain the counterparty registration document. The tax application may be completed online using the certificate of incorporation, articles and proof of registered office. The foreign trade registration authorizes the Company to issue foreign currency export and import declarations for surplus commercial aircraft parts. If any strategic dual-use item is identified in a consignment, a separate export/import permit must be obtained before shipment. The statutory processes run concurrently; the SLA begins upon complete submission and ends after the taxpayer identification and trade registration code have been issued. Any rejection for missing documents must be cured by resubmission within 15 working days.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or title proof
Company seal authorization and officer identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or trade registration is delayed because of document insufficiency, the Company may resubmit within 15 days; a wrong rejection can be appealed to the Finance Ministry or the Bureau of Foreign Trade, as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Aviation Supplier Authorization, Municipal Fire Clearance and Occupational Safety Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Aeronautics Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan; local Fire Bureau; municipal Department of Economic Development; and the Ministry of Labor, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before physical distribution and warehousing operations begin, the Company must obtain the building safety-use license and the fire safety equipment inspection certificate from the local Fire Bureau. The Civil Aeronautics Administration or its authorized audit body must confirm the traceability and airworthiness certification process for certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus; if the Company imports and re-releases parts with Authorized Release Certificates, it must be added to the applicable approved supplier register. A full Civil Defense fire inspection is required once the racking layout and hazardous-material storage points are finalized. The warehouse must demonstrate compliance with occupational safety standards for racking load capacity, forklift traffic, electrical installations and manual handling. A negative fire inspection triggers a reinspection after physical correction; a CAA compliance finding may be rectified by providing corrected release documentation and revising the internal quality control manual.
required_dossiers: Fire safety equipment plan and maintenance records
Warehouse floor plan with racking loads
Civil Aircraft Parts traceability and Authorized Release Certificate procedure manual
Forklift and electrical installation inspection reports
Environmental registration, if hazardous waste thresholds are triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Bureau refuses clearance, the Company may correct structural and suppression deficiencies and request a reinspection; if the CAA questions airworthiness documentation, the Company must revise its internal control procedure and file a corrective action plan with supporting release certificates.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Civil Aeronautics Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan; Bureau of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; local municipal Economic Development Bureau; and the local Fire Bureau
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Civil Aviation Component Distribution Supplier Authorization and Foreign Trade Registration for Aircraft Parts Importation and Exportation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a Full Environmental Impact Assessment for non-manufacturing wholesale distribution and warehousing of civil aircraft parts; a conditional Environmental Registration may be triggered only if the facility stores hazardous chemicals above 1,000 litres or generates hazardous waste above 20 kilograms per month.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from component washing and floor maintenance must comply with Taiwan Effluent Standards of pH 6 to 9, biochemical oxygen demand BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand COD not exceeding 100 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L. No uncontrolled volatile organic compound VOCs emissions are permitted; any degreasing or solvent-based operations must install abatement that does not allow fugitive VOC emissions in excess of 0.6 kg/hr from a single source. Hazardous wastes, including spent solvents, hydraulic fluids and battery electrolyte, must be labelled, stored for no more than 180 days, and removed by a licensed hazardous waste transporter, and the small-quantity generator threshold of 20 kg/month determines the required monthly reporting and manifest obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The warehouse must obtain the Fire Services Act Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Certificate, the Building Safety-Use License, and a Civil Defense Fire Safety Inspection confirming automatic fire alarms, emergency lighting, extinguishers and, where required, automatic sprinkler coverage. The structure must pass a load inspection for high-density racking. The Ministry of Labor and the municipal labor authority must approve the occupational safety management plan covering forklift traffic, rack stability, electrical safety and manual handling procedures, and a certified workplace safety officer must be appointed for the distribution and warehousing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; national Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal administered by STA and competent local tax service offices
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN_WFOE_LTD is formed as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability enterprise under PRC company law. The foreign parent must first register the WFOE with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), which issues the business license and the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is the single statutory taxpayer identification number and serves as both the TIN and VAT registration identifier. Within 30 days after business license issuance, the WFOE must complete tax registration on the STA

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi is generally convertible on the current account for genuine trade and service transactions, with banks performing document-based verification under SAFE's post-supervision system, but the currency remains largely non-convertible on the capital account without specific regulatory approvals. A Taiwan-invested WFOE must first complete SAFE's foreign direct investment registration to obtain a Foreign Exchange Business Registration and Investment Certificate; only then can the offshore shareholder remit capital into the entity's FDI capital settlement account. Inward capital must be settled under the Negative List framework and cannot be used for unapproved domestic equity investments, speculative purposes, or non-operating outflows. Profit and dividend remittances are treated as current account outward transfers only after the WFOE demonstrates audited retained earnings, payment of corporate income tax, and a genuine dividend resolution; banks typically require the annual tax filing, auditor report, and a non-resident witholding tax clearance certificate. Remittances are also governed by the Regulation on Foreign Exchange Administration, and each transfer must carry the appropriate purpose code and be supported by underlying contracts and invoices. There is no central-bank approval requirement for routine genuine profit repatriation, but any mismatch between declared purpose and actual payment, round-tripping red flags, or use of shell companies will trigger enhanced due diligence and possible suspension of the bank's facilitation role. Overall, the current account is open and freely convertible on a documentary basis, while the capital account is gated; the operative hurdle for the WFOE is documentary compliance rather than an explicit quantitative profit remittance quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's goods trade foreign exchange monitoring rules, export proceeds in foreign currency must be received through a domestic designated forex bank and reported to the Customs and SAFE reporting systems. Where no abnormal monitoring category applies, export receipts should be repatriated to China within 90 days from the date of customs clearance. The exporter may elect either to retain the proceeds in a domestic current-account foreign exchange account or to convert them into RMB, with no statutory mandatory percentage conversion ratio. If conversion is elected, the bank applies the prevailing market rate; if retention is elected, the retained foreign currency may only be used for genuine current-account payments and working capital needs. SAFE may assign a trade-inspection category of B or C to exporters showing abnormal collection patterns, which removes simplification privileges and requires full documentary exhaustion for every transaction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: NOT VIABLE as a primary Chinese treasury rail. Under the PRC Licensing Measures for Payment Institutions and SAFE's cross-border forex rules, an offshore digital EMI without a Chinese payment institution license cannot legally open a domestic RMB account for a WFOE, cannot accept instructions from the FDI capital account, and cannot execute corporate forex conversion. Such EMIs may support ancillary merchant collection for non-regulated cross-border flows, but the WFOE's statutory foreign exchange, capital verification, export proceeds, and profit remittance transactions must be processed through a licensed domestic commercial bank. Feasibility rating: Low; use only as a supplementary collection tool when the EMI is backed by a Chinese licensed clearing bank and never for capital account, export surrender, or SAFE-reportable flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For tier-1 Chinese commercial banks, the statutory legal representative must appear physically at a mainland China branch for at least one face-to-face account opening interview and KYC verification. If the legal representative is unable to travel, the mainland-appointed financial controller or senior officer may appear with a notarized board resolution, original power of attorney, and the legal representative's certified identity documents, but pure remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted. Foreign corporate documents from Taiwan must be notarized, accompanied by a certified Chinese translation, and, where applicable, routed through the approved cross-strait document authentication channel. The bank will also require the original business license, seal/company chop, articles of association, board minutes, and UBO identification before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership opacity: a Taiwan shareholder sits behind a mainland WFOE, and the ultimate controller is not a named statutory director or shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Taiwan parent company registration and director list; full group organisational chart; notarised share register; beneficial ownership declaration naming every individual with 25% or greater interest; WFOE articles of association; board resolutions approving the account opening; passport or national ID of every UBO; audited financial statements and source-of-funds evidence of the Taiwan parent; Chinese investment approval certificate and SAFE FDI registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation surplus parts sanctions and export-control exposure: dual-use, military-listed, or regulated civil aviation rotables may implicate PRC, Taiwan, EASA, FAA, or CAAC equipment controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: US/CCL ECCN classification code and Chinese Customs HS classification for each part family; manufacturers' certificates of airworthiness such as EASA Form 1, FAA 8130-3, CAAC AAC-038, or equivalent; end-user certificate and aircraft operator verification; denied-party and entity-list screening logs for all counterparties; supplier invoices showing country of origin; internal export-compliance policy signed by the compliance officer; and a restricted-party screening report generated by the opening bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering through over- or under-invoicing of surplus rotables, especially where valuation of used aviation parts is subjective.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent appraisal reports from a certified aviation appraiser; benchmark pricing from ILS, PartsBase, or OEM price sheets; full trade file including purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, airway bill or bill of lading, customs declarations, and insurance certificates; evidence of payment terms consistent with bank records; and, where sales are to related parties, a full transfer-pricing study under Chinese and OECD principles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account misuse or round-tripping: attempted use of the operating current account to receive shareholder capital or to disguise shareholder loans as trade flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate; bank-issued capital contribution confirmation or capital verification statement; Swift MT103 remittance slips with exact purpose code and remitter name; board minutes recording capital injection; signed shareholder loan agreements where applicable; Chinese corporate tax filings with withholding tax certificates; and a bank reconciliation tracing each tranche from the FDI capital account into permitted operational expenditure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be routed from the Taiwan shareholder's bank account through a direct Swift MT103 to the WFOE's FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account at a Chinese tier-1 bank, referencing the SAFE FDI registration certificate number and the correct capital-account purpose code for foreign direct investment. The WFOE must present the Foreign Investment Certificate, SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration, board resolution, and executed capital contribution agreement before the bank will credit the account. After receipt, the bank conducts capital verification through the electronic FDI registration platform and issues a capital verification statement. Once verified, the capital can be settled into RMB only through the designated RMB capital expenditure account, and the resulting funds must be applied strictly within the approved business scope and Negative List limitations. Use of an omnibus or pooled account is prohibited for FDI capital injection; all transfers must carry a unique end-to-end transaction reference.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE may settle genuine import transactions for surplus commercial aircraft parts using SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments and urgent disbursements once the customs declaration, invoice, and forex purpose code have been uploaded to the bank. For large OEM or high-value rotable purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit at sight is recommended because it provides conditional security of payment and a fully trade-documented clearing rail. Documentary Collections under D/P or D/A terms are permissible and can be used for trusted repeat counterparties, but they carry higher settlement timing risk and require purchase order, inspection certificate, and transport document matching. Every outbound MT103 must include a unique end-to-end transaction reference, the exact beneficiary bank BIC, invoice and air waybill references, the applicable SAFE trade-code, and must pass real-time sanctions, PEP, and denied-party screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts with genuine current-account or capital-account exposure, booked at a Chinese tier-1 bank after confirming the underlying trade documents.
Onshore RMB foreign exchange swaps of spot-forward combination used for short-term liquidity conversion, limited to documented trade or financing flows.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-dated USD/RMB exposure matching an approved foreign currency financing or large capital expenditure commitment.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore by an overseas affiliate are not a permissible onshore PRC treasury product and cannot be booked by the WFOE; onshore NDFs are prohibited, and any use of offshore NDFs must reside outside the mainland legal entity with no SAFE reporting implication.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investor Annual Report (Annual Operations Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June for the preceding calendar year, within six months after the 31 December fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, or filing with materially incorrect ultimate-ownership data, may cause MOEA to issue a 30-day correction order; continued breach can suspend foreign-exchange and dividend-remittance privileges, impose administrative fines per order, and ultimately revoke the foreign-investment approval, triggering administrative forfeiture of the WFOE registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return and Audited Financial Statement Attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (MOF), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May to 31 May immediately following the tax year; a non-calendar-year company must file by the last day of the fifth month after its fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers monthly surcharges of 1% of unpaid tax, capped at 10-15%, plus per-day delinquent-tax interest; material underreporting or failure to file enables tax authority assessment and penalties up to twice the evaded tax; continued non-payment and inactivity for six or more months may lead MOEA to administratively strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval at Shareholders Meeting and Filing with Company Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Authority of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA Company Registration Filing System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders meeting must be held no later than 30 June; approved financial statements, earnings-distribution plan, and board resolutions must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after shareholder approval, creating a hard annual window ending by mid-July for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined NT$10,000-NT$50,000 for each failure to convene or file, escalating to NT$50,000-NT$100,000 for repeated breaches; after two correction orders and continued non-compliance, the competent authority may commence administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Civil Aviation Parts Trading Permit - Annual Compliance Status Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA), Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the permit anniversary date; for mid-year permit issuance, declaration of prior-year sales, inventory age, certified traceability data, and import activity must be submitted within 30 days after each anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or failure to maintain certified surplus-aircraft-parts traceability results in permit suspension, prohibition of importation of aviation parts, and civil penalties under civil aviation regulations; unlicensed or unapproved continued trading constitutes an administrative forfeiture event that terminates customs release privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: On-Site Statutory Register Audit and Annual Corporate Secretary Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary; copy retained with MOEA if any share transfer or charge is recorded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual shareholders meeting on or before 30 June, the corporate secretary must audit the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges, and Minute Book and certify consistency with the audited financial statements as of the prior 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Uncertified register files constitute a statutory governance breach; material inconsistencies require the board to convene within 15 days; unresolved register defects can block company-registration filings, trigger director fines, and expose individual officers to civil liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20, a mandatory independent CPA audit is required where the company's paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000; where the company is publicly listed, OTC-listed, or has obtained a public-offering approval; where MOEA, the Civil Aeronautics Administration, or the banking/escrow AML supervisor imposes an audit covenant because annual aircraft-parts turnover exceeds NT$120,000,000 or full-time headcount exceeds 100; or where the aviation-parts distribution permit expressly requires audited financial statements regardless of paid-in capital. A WFOE below these thresholds may still be designated for statutory audit by MOEA if books are suspected of being materially incomplete or inaccurate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public foreign-invested companies in Taiwan prepare statutory financial statements under the Business Entity Accounting Act and Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS), or the MOEA-approved non-public-company accounting standards; publicly held and FSC-regulated entities apply IFRS as endorsed in Taiwan. Audit opinions must state the accounting framework used and confirm compliance with the company's articles of incorporation, the Company Act, and the licensing conditions of the Civil Aeronautics Administration.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate public UBO register filing; the Ultimate Beneficial Owner confirmation is embedded in the annual Foreign Investor Annual Report and in the annual financial statement board declaration. Any transfer of shares, any change in direct or indirect ownership, or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed with the MOEA Investment Commission within 30 days of the event, and the statutory Register of Members must be contemporaneously annotated. For medium-risk aviation escrow and SWIFT wire operations, enhanced due diligence records identifying the UBO must be retained for at least seven years and refreshed on each annual compliance declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 650-1,500 per year for a Taipei registered-office and corporate-secretary service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000-10,000 per statutory audit by a licensed Taiwan CPA for a mid-size non-public aviation-parts WFOE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for PRC WFOEs; qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises may obtain 15% preferential CIT; small low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income within statutory thresholds may enjoy an effective 5% rate; R&D expenses qualify for an additional 100% super deduction (200% total deduction); certain encouraged industries in free trade zones or Hainan Free Trade Port may access a 15% rate where applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return - A Class), e-filed through the PRC State Taxation Administration electronic taxation portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with quarterly estimated prepayment filings
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (by May 31 of the following year); quarterly estimated returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Tax Residency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, taxpayer identification number (USCC), registered address, legal representative, tax registration type and industry code 4659
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must file as a PRC resident enterprise, not as a foreign enterprise branch; disclose Taiwan shareholder ownership in equity schedules; attach the Taiwan shareholder Tax Residency Certificate only when claiming Cross-Strait DTA relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Accounting Basis, Fiscal Year and Currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period, accrual basis, functional currency, accounting standards applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record all aviation parts sales in RMB using the official spot exchange rate; any transaction routed through a Taiwan intermediary must be priced on an arm's length basis and fully disclosed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting revenue to taxable revenue; add deemed sales, non-exempt subsidies, foreign exchange gains and intercompany reallocations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If surplus commercial aircraft parts are contractually sold by the WFOE but shipped directly from supplier to customer, the entire sales margin is taxable to the WFOE; commission-only arrangements must be supported by contracts and actual functions performed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Deductible Expenses and Intercompany Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report COGS, operating expenses, interest, royalties, management fees, entertainment limits, depreciation, bad debts and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the Taiwan shareholder for services, royalties or interest are deductible only with real economic substance and supporting documentation; interest deduction is limited by the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization rule; intercompany management fees must meet arm's length standards

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforward from prior years, current-year loss computation, and addback of artificial losses from transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for 5 years only; losses created by inflated intercompany purchases from Taiwan affiliates will be disallowed; document commercial reasons for aviation spares inventory write-offs

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable Income and Applicable Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute total taxable income after permanent and temporary differences; apply the standard 25% rate or an eligible preferential rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is a shell without local employees, board meetings or parts inventory in China, tax authorities may recharacterize it as a non-resident permanent establishment and tax profits accordingly; maintain substantive management and CIGA records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Prepaid Tax and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter quarterly prepayments, taxes paid abroad on the same income, and withholding tax credits against PRC CIT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taiwan-source income may be eligible for foreign tax credit only if the Cross-Strait double taxation agreement applies and the Taiwan shareholder/Taiwan tax credit is properly certified; no double counting of treaty relief is permitted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Final Tax Payable and Dividend Withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT payable or refundable after prepayments; separately report profit distributions to non-resident shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend remittance to a Taiwan shareholder generally triggers 10% WHT; to use a reduced 5% treaty rate the Taiwan shareholder must file a beneficial ownership declaration and a current Tax Residency Certificate before any distribution; otherwise the WFOE must withhold 10% and file a withholding tax return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty from RMB 2,000 up to RMB 20,000 for serious cases; late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day; underpayment due to evasion attracts a fine of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; criminal tax fraud is triggered under Criminal Law Article 201 when the amount of tax evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax payable
